question: In view of the increasing pressure on the European Union budget – caused by the increase in the number and cost of EU programmes and the need to repay the debt stemming from the NextGenerationEU instrument – it is particularly important that efficient and economical management of the funds allocated to the Union’s administration be ensured.
One important element of this expenditure is the costs of maintaining, modernising, renting and managing the buildings used by the EU institutions, bodies and agencies. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission have an aggregated analysis of the evolution of the administrative costs borne by the Commission, its bodies and agencies between 2014 and 2025, or any other longer period, detailing expenditure on salaries, property maintenance, rent, renovation, security and energy consumption?

Has the Commission carried out an assessment of the extent to which buildings owned by the Commission and its agencies have been used, in particular now that hybrid working has become more widespread, and have any cost-saving options through the consolidation of office space, the sale of unused property or the abandonment of part of rental contracts been identified?

Does the Commission intend to present to Parliament a comprehensive strategy for the rationalisation of administrative costs, including measurable targets for reducing expenditure on buildings and increasing their efficient use?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) 1. For the Commission, all details on administrative expenditure are available in each annual Draft Budget in the following documents: - Working Document II for the human resources; - Working Document VI for the administrative expenditure under Heading 7; - Working Document VII for the Commission buildings1.

The detailed expenditure, including administrative costs, of both executive and decentralised agencies, as well as Joint Undertakings, can be found in Working Document III accompanying each individual Draft Budget. 2. The Commission continuously assesses its building portfolio to ensure that it remains both cost-effective and energy efficient.

Since 2021, the Commission has been progressively consolidating its services into fewer buildings, phasing out inefficient premises, and refurbishing others for more intensive use through dynamic collaborative spaces. In that context, the Commission sold 23 buildings. 3.

Working Document VII, adopted by the Commission and presented to the budgetary authority along the Draft Budget, features the situation of the buildings in the medium term (up to 2034 in Draft Budget 2027), i.e. the building policy. This includes expenditure and surface, expected evolution of the global surface and final terms and costs.

The Commission forecasts a decrease of its office space from 788 404 square meters (sqm) in 2021 to 563 129 sqm in 2034, which represents more than 25% decrease. These and other measures to rationalise administrative expenditure have been presented and discussed with the European Parliament in the context of the annual draft budgets and negotiations for the next multiannual financial framework (MFF).
